newsitem.title: LEBANON: SLA militiamen, Israeli hurt in Hizbollah attack.
newsitem.headline: SLA militiamen, Israeli hurt in Hizbollah attack.

text.p: Four pro-Israeli militiamen and an Israeli soldier were wounded on Monday when Hizbollah guerrillas attacked their outpost in Lebanon, pro-Israeli militia sources said.
Later, Israeli warplanes struck twice in the area facing the outpost, firing six rockets into suspected Hizbollah bases in the hills of Sojoud and Akmata, Lebanese security sources said.

The South Lebanon Army (SLA) militiamen and the Israeli soldier were injured in fighting with Hizbollah guerrillas who stormed into the outpost of Sojoud on the edge of Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone, the pro-Israeli sources added.

This brought to 28 and 22 respectively the number of Israeli soldiers and SLA militiamen wounded in guerrilla attacks since the start of the year. Six Israeli soldiers and five SLA members were killed over the same period.
Two Hizbollah guerrillas were killed near the entrance of the outpost after planting flags on the position, SLA sources said.
In Beirut, Hizbollah said they had no information on guerrilla casualties.
There were no reports of casualties in the air raid -- the 27th on Lebanon in 1997.

"In the details of the (outpost) attack, the group of April War Martyrs stormed into the outpost of Sojoud where the group of Qana Martyrs advanced and blew off the implanted barriers causing a hole in the outpost's defences," a statement by Hizbollah said.

"Simultaneously, the group of Mansouri Martyrs opened a similar hole on another side of its fortifications. In great speed, the two groups infiltrated into the outpost and cleared it with rocket propelled grenades, machineguns and explosive bombs," the statement added.
Hizbollah guerrillas regularly attack Israeli troops trying to oust them from the south Lebanon occupation zone, which Israel says protects its northern border.

"We warn the enemy against any response that might touch civilians and call on resistance fighters to stay comletely alert against any such act aimed at covering this bitter loss suffered by the Zionist enemy," the statement added.
